stem: Cobalt Freight runs self-managed Oracle databases and wants to remove commercial engine licensing cost, accepting schema and application query rework across a multi-quarter project.

choices.text: Move to Oracle on Amazon EC2, keeping the same engine and its current licensing profile.
Move to Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition and keep the existing SQL dialect unchanged.
Move to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and plan schema, data type, and query conversion.
Move to PostgreSQL and rely on AWS DMS alone to convert stored procedures and application SQL.

rationale: Oracle to PostgreSQL is a heterogeneous migration: the engine changes, so the commercial licensing cost goes away, and schema, data type, and application query conversion become first-class project work. Self-managing Oracle on Amazon EC2 is a homogeneous move that keeps the same engine and therefore the same licensing profile. Moving to Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition is also a heterogeneous move, so SQL dialect and data type differences still have to be evaluated rather than assumed to carry over. AWS DMS moves data between endpoints and does not by itself convert stored procedures or application SQL, so a heterogeneous move still needs separate schema and code conversion work.
